title.en: Purpose and Result (to / so that / so … that / such … that / too … to)
title.es: Finalidad y resultado (to / so that / so … that / such … that / too … to)

text.en: Purpose says why we do something; result says what came of it. Purpose: to + base verb (“I went to the store to buy milk.”), in order to, so as to, when the subject is the same, and so that + clause, mostly with a different subject (also with the same subject plus can/will/would) (“I speak slowly so that you can understand.”). Result: so, therefore, as a result, consequently, and so + adjective + that and such + (a) + noun + that. The Spanish “para”, “para que”, “por lo tanto”, “tan … que” match them.
text.es: La finalidad dice para qué hacemos algo; el resultado dice qué salió de ello. Finalidad: to + verbo base («I went to the store to buy milk.»), in order to, so as to, cuando el sujeto es el mismo, y so that + cláusula, sobre todo con otro sujeto (también con el mismo sujeto más can/will/would) («I speak slowly so that you can understand.»). Resultado: so, therefore, as a result, consequently, además de so + adjetivo + that y such + (a) + sustantivo + that. El «para», el «para que», el «por lo tanto» y el «tan … que» del español les corresponden.

rows: para que (cláusula con can / will / would)

title.en: Purpose with the same subject: to, in order to, so as to
title.es: Finalidad con el mismo sujeto: to, in order to, so as to

text.en: To + base verb is the most common; in order to and so as to are more formal. Negative: in order not to, so as not to.
text.es: To + verbo base es lo más común; in order to y so as to son más formales. Negación: in order not to, so as not to.

examples.es: I went to the store to buy milk.

tr.en: I went to the store to buy milk.
tr.es: Fui a la tienda para comprar leche.

examples.es: She whispered so as not to wake the baby.

tr.en: She whispered so as not to wake the baby.
tr.es: Susurró para no despertar al bebé.

text.en: For goes before a noun or an -ing form, not before a base verb: “for a loan”, “a knife is for cutting”. Not “for buy”.
text.es: For va antes de un sustantivo o una forma -ing, no antes de un verbo base: «for a loan», «a knife is for cutting». No «for buy».

examples.es: I went to the bank for a loan.

tr.en: I went to the bank for a loan.
tr.es: Fui al banco por un préstamo.

tr.en: A knife is for cutting.
tr.es: Un cuchillo sirve para cortar.

title.en: Purpose with a clause: so that
title.es: Finalidad con una cláusula: so that

text.en: After so that come a subject and a verb, with can/will for the present or future and could/would for the past: “She left early so that she wouldn’t be late.” It also works with the same subject when can/will/would is needed.
text.es: Después de so that van un sujeto y un verbo, con can/will para el presente o futuro y could/would para el pasado: «She left early so that she wouldn’t be late.» También sirve con el mismo sujeto cuando hace falta can/will/would.

examples.es: I speak slowly so that you can understand me.

tr.en: I speak slowly so that you can understand me.
tr.es: Hablo despacio para que me entiendas.

examples.es: She left early so that she wouldn't be late.

tr.en: She left early so that she wouldn't be late.
tr.es: Salió temprano para no llegar tarde.

examples.es: I am learning English so that I can get a better job.

tr.en: I am learning English so that I can get a better job.
tr.es: Estoy aprendiendo inglés para poder conseguir un mejor trabajo.

title.en: Result: so, therefore, as a result, consequently
title.es: Resultado: so, therefore, as a result, consequently

text.en: So is common in speech; therefore, as a result and consequently are used in writing, at the start of a new sentence, with a comma.
text.es: So es común al hablar; therefore, as a result y consequently se usan al escribir, al inicio de una oración nueva, con coma.

examples.es: It rained all day. As a result, the game was canceled.

tr.en: It rained all day. As a result, the game was canceled.
tr.es: Llovió todo el día. Como resultado, se canceló el partido.

examples.es: He didn't study. Therefore, he failed.

tr.en: He didn't study. Therefore, he failed.
tr.es: No estudió. Por lo tanto, reprobó.

text.en: So + adjective or adverb + that: “so cold that”. Such + (a) + noun + that: “such a cold day that”. Such always goes with a noun. For quantities use so many / so much + noun + that: “so many people that”; with an uncountable noun there is no a: “such good news”.
text.es: So + adjetivo o adverbio + that: «so cold that». Such + (a) + sustantivo + that: «such a cold day that». Such siempre va con un sustantivo. Para cantidades se usa so many / so much + sustantivo + that: «so many people that»; con un sustantivo incontable no hay a: «such good news».

examples.es: It was so cold that we stayed in.

tr.en: It was so cold that we stayed in.
tr.es: Hacía tanto frío que nos quedamos adentro.

examples.es: It was such a cold day that we stayed in.

tr.en: It was such a cold day that we stayed in.
tr.es: Fue un día tan frío que nos quedamos adentro.

examples.es: There were so many people that we could not move.

tr.en: There were so many people that we could not move.
tr.es: Había tanta gente que no podíamos movernos.

text.en: Too + adjective + to: too much to. Adjective + enough + to: enough to.
text.es: Too + adjetivo + to: demasiado para. Adjetivo + enough + to: lo bastante para.

examples.es: She is too tired to study.

tr.en: She is too tired to study.
tr.es: Está demasiado cansada para estudiar.

examples.es: He is old enough to vote.

tr.en: He is old enough to vote.
tr.es: Ya tiene edad suficiente para votar.

text.en: Spanish influence: not “I went to the store for buy milk”. The Spanish “para” + verb is to + base verb in English. For can only stand before a noun or an -ing form.
text.es: Influencia del español: no «I went to the store for buy milk». El «para» + verbo del español es to + verbo base en inglés. For solo puede ir antes de un sustantivo o una forma -ing.

text.en: The Spanish “tan … que” is so … that in English, and “tal … que” is such … that. So goes with an adjective, such with a noun: “so tired”, but “such a tired man”.
text.es: El «tan … que» del español es so … that en inglés, y «tal … que» es such … that. So va con un adjetivo, such con un sustantivo: «so tired», pero «such a tired man».

speak.en: Purpose says why we do something. With the same subject: «to» plus the base verb, or more formally «in order to». With a clause, mostly a different subject: «so that» plus a clause: «I speak slowly so that you can understand». «For» only goes before a noun or an -ing form. Result: «therefore» and «as a result» at the start of a new sentence. «So cold that» with an adjective, «such a cold day that» with a noun. «Too tired to study» and «old enough to vote».
speak.es: La finalidad dice para qué hacemos algo. Con el mismo sujeto: «to» más verbo base, o más formal «in order to». Con una cláusula, sobre todo con otro sujeto: «so that» más una cláusula: «I speak slowly so that you can understand». «For» solo va antes de un sustantivo o una forma -ing. Resultado: «therefore» y «as a result» al inicio de una oración nueva. «So cold that» con un adjetivo, «such a cold day that» con un sustantivo. «Too tired to study» y «old enough to vote».

gloss.en: but, in spite of the fact

items.sentence: There were so ___ people that we could not move.

why.en: Before a countable plural noun comes so many: so many people that.
why.es: Antes de un sustantivo contable en plural va so many: so many people that.

much.en: So much goes with uncountable nouns; people is countable.
much.es: So much va con sustantivos incontables; people es contable.

such.en: Such does not replace so in this structure; you need so many.
such.es: Such no reemplaza a so en esta estructura; hace falta so many.

examples: There were so many cars that we waited.
She has so many books that she sells some.

tr.en: There were so many people that we could not move.
tr.es: Había tanta gente que no podíamos movernos.

items.sentence: She studies hard ___ order to pass the exam.

why.en: A formal purpose: in order to.
why.es: Una finalidad formal: in order to.

for.en: “For order to” does not exist; you need in order to.
for.es: «For order to» no existe; hace falta in order to.

at.en: “At order to” does not exist; you need in order to.
at.es: «At order to» no existe; hace falta in order to.

examples: He works in order to live.
We left early in order to win.

tr.en: She studies hard in order to pass the exam.
tr.es: Ella estudia mucho para pasar el examen.

items.sentence: He left early ___ as not to be late.

why.en: A negative purpose: so as not to.
why.es: Una finalidad negativa: so as not to.

in.en: “In as not to” does not exist; you need in order not to or so as not to.
in.es: «In as not to» no existe; hace falta in order not to o so as not to.

for.en: “For as not to” does not exist; you need so as not to.
for.es: «For as not to» no existe; hace falta so as not to.

examples: She spoke softly so as not to wake him.
I ran so as not to miss it.

tr.en: He left early so as not to be late.
tr.es: Él se fue temprano para no llegar tarde.

items.sentence: I speak slowly ___ you can understand me.

why.en: A different subject and a clause: so that + you can.
why.es: Otro sujeto y una cláusula: so that + you can.

in order to.en: After in order to comes a base verb, not a subject and verb (you can).
in order to.es: Después de in order to va un verbo base, no sujeto y verbo (you can).

for.en: After for comes a noun or an -ing form, not a subject and verb.
for.es: Después de for va un sustantivo o una forma -ing, no sujeto y verbo.

examples: Speak up so that he can hear.
Write it so that we remember.

tr.en: I speak slowly so that you can understand me.
tr.es: Hablo despacio para que me entiendas.

items.sentence: She left early so that she ___ be late.

why.en: A purpose in the past: so that + wouldn’t.
why.es: Una finalidad en el pasado: so that + wouldn’t.

didn't.en: “Didn’t be late” is not correct; after so that a modal verb is needed (wouldn’t).
didn't.es: «Didn’t be late» no es correcto; después de so that hace falta un verbo modal (wouldn’t).

doesn't.en: Doesn’t is present, and after so that a modal verb is needed.
doesn't.es: Doesn’t es presente, y después de so that hace falta un verbo modal.

examples: He hurried so that he would not miss it.
She ran so that she could catch it.

tr.en: She left early so that she wouldn't be late.
tr.es: Ella se fue temprano para no llegar tarde.

why.en: The use of an object: for + -ing.
why.es: El uso de un objeto: for + -ing.

to.en: “To cutting” is not correct; before an -ing form comes for.
to.es: «To cutting» no es correcto; antes de una forma -ing va for.

so.en: “So cutting” is not correct; before an -ing form comes for.
so.es: «So cutting» no es correcto; antes de una forma -ing va for.

examples: A pen is for writing.
A key is for opening.

tr.en: A knife is for cutting.
tr.es: Un cuchillo es para cortar.

items.sentence: It was ___ good news that she cried.

why.en: Before an uncountable noun comes such (without a): such good news.
why.es: Antes de un sustantivo incontable va such (sin a): such good news.

so.en: So goes before an adjective; before a noun you need such.
so.es: So va antes de un adjetivo; antes de un sustantivo hace falta such.

too.en: “Too good news” is not correct here; before a noun you need such.
too.es: «Too good news» no es correcto aquí; antes de un sustantivo hace falta such.

examples: It was such nice weather that we swam.
She gave such good advice that I stayed.

tr.en: It was such good news that she cried.
tr.es: Fue una noticia tan buena que ella lloró.

items.sentence: It rained all day. ___, the game was canceled.

why.en: A result at the start of a new sentence: As a result,
why.es: Un resultado al inicio de una oración nueva: As a result,

Because.en: Because introduces a reason and needs a clause; it does not stand before a comma.
Because.es: Because introduce una razón y necesita una cláusula; no va antes de una coma.

In order.en: In order does not stand alone; you need in order to + base verb.
In order.es: In order no va solo; hace falta in order to + verbo base.

examples: It snowed. As a result, we stayed.
He lost. As a result, he cried.

tr.en: It rained all day. As a result, the game was canceled.
tr.es: Llovió todo el día. Como resultado, el juego se canceló.

why.en: A result at the start of a new sentence: Therefore,
why.es: Un resultado al inicio de una oración nueva: Therefore,

Although.en: Although marks a contrast, not a result.
Although.es: Although marca un contraste, no un resultado.

Despite.en: Despite marks a contrast and is followed by a noun or an -ing form.
Despite.es: Despite marca un contraste y lo sigue un sustantivo o una forma -ing.

examples: It was late. Therefore, we left.
She won. Therefore, she smiled.

tr.en: He didn't study. Therefore, he failed.
tr.es: Él no estudió. Por lo tanto, reprobó.

items.sentence: It was ___ cold that we stayed in.

why.en: Before an adjective comes so: so cold that.
why.es: Antes de un adjetivo va so: so cold that.

such.en: Such goes with a noun (such a cold day); not before a bare adjective.
such.es: Such va con un sustantivo (such a cold day); no antes de un adjetivo solo.

too.en: “Too cold that” is not correct; after too comes to + base verb.
too.es: «Too cold that» no es correcto; después de too va to + verbo base.

examples: It was so hot that I left.
She was so tired that she slept.

tr.en: It was so cold that we stayed in.
tr.es: Hacía tanto frío que nos quedamos adentro.

items.sentence: It was ___ a cold day that we stayed in.

why.en: Before a noun comes such: such a cold day that.
why.es: Antes de un sustantivo va such: such a cold day that.

so.en: “So a cold day” is not correct; before a noun you need such.
so.es: «So a cold day» no es correcto; antes de un sustantivo hace falta such.

too.en: “Too a cold day” is not correct; before a noun you need such.
too.es: «Too a cold day» no es correcto; antes de un sustantivo hace falta such.

examples: It was such a big house that we got lost.
She is such a kind person.

tr.en: It was such a cold day that we stayed in.
tr.es: Fue un día tan frío que nos quedamos adentro.

why.en: More than needed for: too + adjective + to.
why.es: Más de lo necesario para: too + adjetivo + to.

so.en: “So tired to study” is not correct; after so comes a that-clause.
so.es: «So tired to study» no es correcto; después de so viene una cláusula con that.

enough.en: Enough goes after the adjective (tired enough), not before it.
enough.es: Enough va después del adjetivo (tired enough), no antes.

examples: He is too young to drive.
It is too hot to work.

tr.en: She is too tired to study.
tr.es: Ella está demasiado cansada para estudiar.

items.sentence: She spoke quietly in order ___ to wake the baby.

why.en: A negative purpose: in order not to + base verb.
why.es: Una finalidad negativa: in order not to + verbo base.

no.en: “In order no to” does not exist; the negative is not.
no.es: «In order no to» no existe; la negación es not.

don't.en: “In order don’t to” does not exist; the negative is not.
don't.es: «In order don’t to» no existe; la negación es not.

examples: He left in order not to be late.
She whispered in order not to wake him.

tr.en: She spoke quietly in order not to wake the baby.
tr.es: Ella habló bajito para no despertar al bebé.

items.sentence: The test was ___ difficult that nobody passed.

why.en: Before an adjective comes so: so difficult that.
why.es: Antes de un adjetivo va so: so difficult that.

such.en: Such goes with a noun (such a difficult test); here before the adjective you need so.
such.es: Such va con un sustantivo (such a difficult test); aquí antes del adjetivo hace falta so.

too.en: “Too difficult that” is not correct; after too comes to + base verb.
too.es: «Too difficult that» no es correcto; después de too va to + verbo base.

examples: The film was so long that I slept.
It was so loud that we left.

tr.en: The test was so difficult that nobody passed.
tr.es: El examen estuvo tan difícil que nadie pasó.

items.sentence: She was ___ a good singer that everyone listened.

why.en: Before a noun comes such: such a good singer.
why.es: Antes de un sustantivo va such: such a good singer.

so.en: “So a good singer” is not correct; before a noun you need such.
so.es: «So a good singer» no es correcto; antes de un sustantivo hace falta such.

too.en: “Too a good singer” is not correct; before a noun you need such.
too.es: «Too a good singer» no es correcto; antes de un sustantivo hace falta such.

examples: He is such a nice man.
It was such a long day.

tr.en: She was such a good singer that everyone listened.
tr.es: Ella era tan buena cantante que todos escucharon.

items.sentence: We left a note ___ that she would know.

why.en: A different subject and a clause: so that she would know.
why.es: Otro sujeto y una cláusula: so that she would know.

in.en: “In that” does not express a purpose in this structure; you need so that.
in.es: «In that» no expresa una finalidad en esta estructura; hace falta so that.

for.en: “For that” does not express a purpose in this structure; you need so that.
for.es: «For that» no expresa una finalidad en esta estructura; hace falta so that.

examples: I wrote it so that you know.
We hid it so that he would not see.

tr.en: We left a note so that she would know.
tr.es: Dejamos una nota para que ella supiera.

items.sentence: The shop was closed. ___, we went home.

why.en: A result at the start of a new sentence: Consequently,
why.es: Un resultado al inicio de una oración nueva: Consequently,

However.en: However marks a contrast, not a result.
However.es: However marca un contraste, no un resultado.

Although.en: Although marks a contrast and introduces a clause.
Although.es: Although marca un contraste e introduce una cláusula.

examples: It was late. Consequently, we left.
He was ill. Consequently, he stayed.

tr.en: The shop was closed. Consequently, we went home.
tr.es: La tienda estaba cerrada. Por consiguiente, nos fuimos a casa.
